transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the August 25 production policy review for the public API rate-limit project, I want to make sure we're all aligned on the process. I'll be making the final decision on the policy that gets communicated to customers, but before I do, I need each of your teams — backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations — to report your release-impacting findings. To recap what's currently in the draft policy: 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, the same limit applied to authentication endpoints, and no specified staffed launch window. Please bring any concerns or findings related to those areas so we can finalize this together.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share a release-impacting finding from backend engineering. While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Our load replay confirms the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. The current draft limit of 100 requests per minute would break legitimate bulk-import workflows. I hadn't updated the draft because the client test was owned by another team, but this is critical for the policy decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from customer success. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that Acme's contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered the clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this contractual notice requirement needs to be factored into the policy decision and customer communication timeline.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from security. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. The current draft applies the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints, which would be insufficient to protect against credential-abuse attacks. This finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but it's critical for the policy decision.
